newsitem.title: UK: Pru H1 profits up as misselling costs rise.
newsitem.headline: Pru H1 profits up as misselling costs rise.

text.p: Britain's largest life insurance company Prudential Corp on Wednesday reported a rise in profits and sales in all its major businesses over the first six months of the year.
Pre-tax operating profits rose to 442 million pounds ($718 million) from 421 million pounds last year.
Excluding income from disposals made in 1996, profits from continuing operations were up 19 percent over the period.
However, the company said it had increased the provision to cover the costs for the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) review into pensions misselling by 210 million pounds to 450 million pounds.
The Pru said it was determined to resolve the issue as quickly as possible and had agreed with the SIB a guarantee to affected customers that they would not suffer any finacial loss.
The provisons would have no impact on bonuses paid to policyholders or statutory profit, said the Pru.
Chief executive Sir Peter Davis said it had been a good year with healthy increases in profits and sales worldwide.
"We have a clear strategy to concentrate our energy and resources on developing our businesses in the UK, U.S., Asia, Australia and New Zealand," said Davis.
Funds under management around the world reached 100 billion pounds.
The Pru increased the dividend by 10.3 percent to 6.4 pence per share which following the changes made in the July budget is to be paid as a foreign income dividend.
In the UK the company's objectives remain to expand its product range and distribution capabilities and building its customer base.
Prudential UK profits rose 16 percent to 197 million pounds with a nine percent increase in life pension and investment business to 170 million pounds.
Prudential banking, launched on October 1 last year, has since attracted 250 million pounds of mortgage applications and 274 million pounds of deposits.
In the U.S., profits from Jackson National Life grew 15 percent to 176 million pounds. Excluding currency factors, profits were up 23 percent. ($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
